questions.question_text:
The inverse variation model $s=\dfrac{180}{t}$ gives the average speed $s$ (km/h) needed to travel $180$ km in time $t$ (hours).
Why is there no point on this graph with $s=0$?

options.text: At zero speed, the car cannot travel $180$ km in any finite time.
Zero speed means the trip takes zero hours.
options.why: Confuses not moving with completing the trip instantly; $s=0$ cannot give $180$ km of travel.

options.text: The graph passes through the origin, so zero speed is possible.
options.why: Treats the inverse variation curve as a direct variation line through the origin.

options.text: The car can complete the trip at zero speed if it waits long enough.
options.why: Assumes waiting produces distance travelled, although at $s=0$ the car does not move.

questions.solution_text:
For any positive finite time $t$, $\dfrac{180}{t}>0$, so $s$ cannot equal $0$.
In this model, a car travelling at zero speed cannot complete the $180$ km trip.
